project.scope: Make the approved Northgate Dental frontend work: accounts, roles, appointment booking and the two dashboards. The design is finished and must not change.

runtime.deploy: static frontend plus a local API process

evidence: rows that survive restarting the application

dataModels.purpose: One row per registered patient or staff member. Email is unique.
An issued session. The cookie carries this id and nothing else about the account.
One appointment request. `status` is requested, confirmed or cancelled. `account_id` is the owner.

apis.purpose: Create an account. Refuses an email that is already registered.
Issue a session for correct credentials. The same 401 for an unknown email and a wrong password.
Who the session belongs to, and the role. The navigation's signed-in shape depends on it.
Record an appointment request from the booking form. Attaches the account when one is signed in.
The signed-in patient's OWN appointments. Never anyone else's.
Cancel an appointment the caller owns. Someone else's is refused with 403, not hidden.
Every appointment, for the practice schedule. A customer session is refused with 403.
Confirm or cancel any appointment. Staff only.

securityControls.requirement: A password is never stored or logged in a form it could be read back from. Only a hash is kept.
evidence: no column holding a plaintext password

securityControls.requirement: Every read and write of an appointment is scoped to the caller's own account, on the server. Filtering in the browser is not authorisation.
evidence: account_id compared against the session on the server

securityControls.requirement: The staff endpoints and the staff page's data are refused to a customer session. Being unlinked in the navigation is not a control.
evidence: a role check on the server before any staff data is returned

securityControls.requirement: The session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite, so a script cannot read it and another site cannot send it.
No credential, hash or session secret appears in anything the browser downloads.
evidence: the built assets contain no secret

operations.behaviour: Create an account from the registration form and sign the person in, showing errors in the form's own style when the email is taken or the password is too short.
acceptance: a valid registration creates exactly one row in accounts with a hashed password
registering an email that already exists is refused with 422 and creates no second row
a password under 12 characters is refused with 422 and nothing is stored
the stored password_hash is not the password

operations.behaviour: Sign in with an email and password, issue a session cookie, and show one message for any failure.
acceptance: correct credentials are accepted and a session cookie is set HttpOnly
a wrong password is refused with 401 and no session is issued
an unknown email is refused with the same 401 and the same message as a wrong password
GET /api/me returns the signed-in account and its role

operations.behaviour: Persist an appointment request and confirm it in the form's own style. Attach it to the signed-in account when there is one.
acceptance: a submitted request is stored as a row in appointments with status 'requested'
a request missing a required field is refused with 422 and nothing is stored
a request made while signed in has account_id set to that account
a storage failure shows an error in the form rather than a false confirmation

operations.behaviour: List the signed-in patient's own appointments in the approved table, and show the approved empty state when there are none.
acceptance: the list contains only appointments whose account_id is the signed-in account
an unauthenticated request is refused with 401
a patient with no appointments sees the empty state, not an error
requesting the list as one patient never returns another patient's row

operations.behaviour: Cancel an appointment the signed-in patient owns, and reflect the new status in the table.
acceptance: cancelling an own appointment sets its status to 'cancelled' and persists
cancelling another account's appointment is refused with 403 and leaves it unchanged
cancelling while unauthenticated is refused with 401
cancelling an already-cancelled appointment does not create a second change

operations.behaviour: List every appointment for the practice schedule, with the approved counts above it.
acceptance: a staff session receives every appointment
a customer session is refused with 403 rather than receiving an empty list
an unauthenticated request is refused with 401
the requested and confirmed counts match the rows actually stored

operations.behaviour: Confirm or cancel any appointment from the schedule, and reflect it in the table and the counts.
acceptance: a staff session can set an appointment to confirmed and the change persists
a customer session attempting the same is refused with 403 and the appointment is unchanged
an unknown status value is refused with 422
the change is visible to the owning patient's own list

outOfScope: No payment is taken and no card details are handled.
No email or SMS is sent: confirmation is shown in the interface only.
No real patient data. No clinical records of any kind.
Nothing is deployed. The finished application runs locally for verification.

missing.what: How a staff account comes to exist
missing.why: Registration creates customers. Promoting an account to staff is an administrative act, and the approved design has no screen for it.
